device_scope: GT-BE19000AI BCM6813 / Brahma-B53; excludes the separate AI board

local_repository.reason: Enable only after actual custom .deb packages and signed Release/InRelease metadata exist; no invented URI or trust bypass.
local_repository.armel_policy: Supply native armel packages from the project repository only. Ubuntu armel-cross packages are build sysroots, not a native armel distribution.

requirements: Use persistent writable storage for installed packages and their database; a writable /usr alone is insufficient.
Do not inherit ASUS whole-/var tmpfs or volatile /etc for dpkg-owned configuration and package state.
Reserve /usr/local for administrator-managed additions; distribute this system's components as .deb packages under /usr.
Keep /lib/ld-linux*.so.* interpreter entries as valid links through usrmerge to the corresponding ABI loader.
The configuration package does not convert paths, create filesystems, or choose/modify any live boot slot.

cpu.isa: ARMv8.0-A with CRC, Crypto and FP/NEON
cpu.build_host_caution: Do not use -march=native on the GB10 build host for router executables.

arm64.role: Native Ubuntu base and new or successfully ported components

armel.role: Existing BCM SDK vendor ABI and source-rebuilt components with vendor dependencies
armel.existing_vendor_blobs: Preserve their actual ABI until a specific interface is audited; architecture alone does not justify a time32 exception for newly built components.

armhf.role: Optional additional packages; current BCM SDK does not require this ABI
armhf.activation: Architecture registration permits later package installation; no armhf runtime is installed by this configuration package.
armhf.time_policy: Use consistent Ubuntu time64/file-offset64 defaults. An exception requires a proven individual legacy boundary and a recorded narrow workaround.

package_policy.ownership: All shipped base, toolchain, runtime and vendor additions must have truthful dpkg ownership/version/dependency metadata. Never overwrite packaged libc with loose files while retaining old package metadata.

glibc.reuse: Use authenticated Ubuntu glibc 2.44-1ubuntu1 source and packaging; reuse BE98 time64/legacy-boundary findings as regression requirements.
glibc.coinstallation: Custom libc6 packages marked Multi-Arch: same for arm64, armel and armhf must carry an identical full Debian version and coinstall cleanly. Their matching development packages and architecture-independent shared files must follow the same version/coownership rules.
glibc.packaging: Rebase Ubuntu/Debian packaging onto pinned upstream source, preserve maintainer scripts, ldconfig triggers, symbols/shlibs and matching libc-bin/libc6-dev/locale dependencies. Signed local repository policy must prevent accidental replacement by an incompatible runtime.
glibc.kernel_assumptions: Keep --enable-kernel=4.19; time64 backports do not justify assuming every API from Linux 5.1 or newer.
glibc.time64: Expose time64 APIs to new/rebuilt applications by default while retaining correctly implemented legacy ABI symbols for existing vendor binaries. Any application-level time32 exception must satisfy time64_policy.
glibc.libc_internal_build: Keep Ubuntu libc internal _DISTRO_EVADE_TIME_BITS and legacy symbol build rules; _TIME_BITS=64 application policy must not erase libc implementations of the old ABI.

gcc.rebuild: Rebuild in Ubuntu/Debian package layout with --enable-multiarch and major-version paths, standard /usr/include and ABI library locations. Remove the BE98 USB build's /opt sysroot/interpreter and USB rpaths. Use separate armel/armhf cross-compiler packages when required; AArch64 GCC -m32 is not an ARM32 compiler.

binutils.packaging: Build Ubuntu/Debian-style native B53 packages and the required separate target cross-binutils; preserve plugin/LTO support and truthful shared-library dependencies. Benchmark link workloads before claiming a performance improvement.

package_policy.vendor_components: Keep closed-source ABI and required hardcoded paths; audit BE19000AI-specific collisions and private plugins before reusing BE98 compatibility links. All kernel modules remain AArch64 and follow kernel Kbuild flags.

systemd.approach: Keep matching Ubuntu source/package family; narrow legacy credential mount fallback required for kernel4.19 after real pidfd backport. Preserve credential access control and read-only ramfs.
systemd.full_acceptance: Must pass full base boot, supplied credentials and apt service transactions before claiming compatibility; ASUS orchestration remains separate.

configuration_package_actions: Install an Ubuntu deb822 source file with explicit supported archive architectures and archive-keyring trust.
Install this informational CPU/ABI/layout/package profile and its package documentation.
On configure, require native dpkg architecture arm64 and register foreign architectures armel and armhf.
acceptance_pending: Build and test the custom glibc/GCC/binutils Debian packages; this profile does not supply them.
Validate package install/upgrade/solver behavior and every enabled ABI in a disposable writable Ubuntu rootfs.
Validate systemd and complete ASUS service integration with the actual kernel9 in QEMU before hardware acceptance.

time64_policy.priority: Use time64 for every new or rebuilt component that can support it; repair source bugs before considering a legacy workaround.
exception_required_evidence: proven time_t/off_t/struct layout or symbol ABI mismatch
narrow repair or compatibility shim attempted first
limited flags or isolated boundary retained if repair is infeasible
positive time64 and legacy regression results
documented exit criteria for removing the exception
time64_policy.legacy_flags_scope: Only the recorded individual component or ABI boundary; never the default for armel, armhf or the entire SDK.
time64_policy.glibc_build_internals: Application time64 defaults must not blindly override libc internal build rules: preserve glibc time32 compatibility symbols for unchanged consumers while exposing time64 to new applications.
time64_policy.raw_syscall_rule: Do not pass libc time64 struct timespec/timeval into legacy time32 syscall numbers. Use libc wrappers or explicitly sized kernel UAPI structures with verified translation.
time64_policy.existing_blob_boundary: Keep unchanged vendor blobs isolated with their existing ABI until interoperation is proven; preserve compatible symbol versions and use checked translation across unavoidable time32 boundaries.

time64_acceptance_matrix.required: Compile and run sizeof(time_t)==8 plus post-2038 timer/file timestamp checks.
Compile with _TIME_BITS=64 and _FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64; assert time_t/off_t==8, confirm exported symbol bindings, and test post-2038 timerfd, utimensat/statx and sparse-file offsets.

Audit BusyBox and rebuilt source for legacy raw clock/time syscalls; test struct offsets and canary tails. Reuse BE98 get_mono repair and verify monotonic progression, ping RTT/deadline and timeout behavior.
Record both sides structure sizes/offsets, integer widths, symbol versions and serialized formats; prove no implicit reinterpretation/truncation before integrating the rebuilt component.
A reproduced, named incompatibility plus narrow fallback test is mandatory. Keep positive time64 tests for other components passing.
Full relocation/loader test in addition to public symbol scans; audit old libcrypt GLIBC_PRIVATE references and rebuild compatible libxcrypt if needed.
Cache-disabled and cached resolution, TLS/pthreads, signals/cancellation/futex waits, DNS/NSS, C++ unwinding and exact ABI loaders.

be98_known_pitfalls.symptom: ARM32 time64 timespec was passed to old clock_gettime syscall; only half the structure was written and ping reported enormous RTTs.
be98_known_pitfalls.resolution: Keep time64 and call libc clock_gettime() under __USE_TIME_BITS64 so glibc handles syscall selection/translation.
be98_known_pitfalls.status: Recorded BE98 hardware success; must be ported/tested against this candidate, not assumed deployed.

be98_known_pitfalls.symptom: Old armel libcrypt required __snprintf@GLIBC_PRIVATE absent from the new glibc.
be98_known_pitfalls.resolution: Rebuild libxcrypt4.4.38 with obsolete ABI support, preserve versioned exports and test DES/MD5 crypt vectors.
be98_known_pitfalls.classification: libc private ABI dependency, not a reason to disable time64.

be98_known_pitfalls.symptom: Ubuntu GCC15 already enables time64 and large-file defaults, unlike earlier build assumptions.
be98_known_pitfalls.resolution: Make defaults explicit for new builds. Earlier broad -U preservation settings are historical; migrate source components to time64 and keep only proven per-component exceptions.
